title: Wolbachia Limits Pathogen Infections Through Induction of Host Innate Immune Responses
author: Lin Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xcafise
materials: RNA sequencing and analysis Total RNA of 15 female mosquitoes of each group was extracted using TRIzol reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific,USA) following the manufacturer’s protocol. cDNA library construction and sequencing were performed according to standard procedures by Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI-Shenzhen, China) using BGISEQ-500 platform. At least 60 Mb clean reads of sequencing were obtained for each sample. Since no genomic sequence in any database was available for Cx. pipiens pallens, Trinity [29] was used to perform de novo assembly with clean reads, then Tgicl [30] was used on cluster transcripts to remove abundance and retain Unigenes. After assembly, Unigenes functional annotation was performed with 7 functional databases (NR, NT, GO, KOG, KEGG, SwissProt and InterPro), then all the clean reads of each sample were mapped to the Unigenes with Bowtie2 [31] software and the gene expression levels were calculated with RSEM [32]. Based on the gene expression levels, the DEGs (differential expression genes) between samples or groups were identified with PossionDis [33] (Fold Change >= 2.00 and FDR<= 0.001). The DEGs were classified based on the GO annotation results and official classification. Pathway analysis was performed to provide further information on the DEGs’ biological functions. The DEGs were also subjected to KEGG pathway classification and functional enrichment.

steps.title: Maintain Mosquito Populations
steps.instruction: Maintain Cx. pipiens pallens larvae in an insectary under specific environmental conditions.

substeps.instruction: Keep mosquitoes at 28°C and 75% relative humidity.
Set photoperiod to 14h light and 10h darkness.
Feed adult mosquitoes 10% (w/v) glucose solution prior to blood meals.

steps.title: Eliminate Wolbachia via Tetracycline Treatment
steps.instruction: Establish Wolbachia-negative Culex populations using tetracycline treatment through larval and pupal stages.

substeps.instruction: Prepare tetracycline (Amresco) solution at a concentration of 0.05 mg/ml.
Place eggs on the tetracycline water solution to hatch.
Transfer surviving larvae to fresh tetracycline solution every 24 hours.
Maintain a parallel control group using a normal infusion.
Continue treatment for 6 generations to establish Wolbachia-negative populations.

steps.title: Establish New Host-Wolbachia Symbiosis
steps.instruction: Perform mating experiments to create specific host-Wolbachia combinations.

substeps.instruction: Place pupae from each population into 15 ml tubes with water for individual emergence to separate virgin females and males.
Raise adult males and females in 30.5×30.5×30.5 cm cages.
Select females 1 day post-eclosion and males 2 days post-eclosion for mating.
Set up crossing groups: NJ♀×TKtet♂, TK♀×NJtet♂, and controls (NJ♀×NJ♂ and TK♀×TK♂).
Allow females and males in the same cages 2 days to mate.
Blood feed females after mating.
Allow egg rafts 48 hours after oviposition to hatch.
Collect females of (NJ♀×TKtet♂)F1, (TK♀×NJtet♂)F1, NJ, and TK 2 days post-eclosion for RNA extraction and sequencing.

steps.title: Perform Microbial Challenge and Survival Experiments
steps.instruction: Challenge 2-day-old female mosquitoes with bacterial cultures.

substeps.instruction: Prepare concentrated overnight bacterial cultures of Gram-negative (Escherichia coli), Gram-positive (Micrococcus luteus), or sterile LB culture (negative control).
Dip an acupuncture needle (0.20×25mm) into the chosen culture.
Prick the mosquitoes in the rear part of the abdomen.
Perform three parallel experiments per group, with 15-20 mosquitoes per container.

description: Validation of immunity-related DEGs by real-time quantitative PCR Total RNA was extracted using TRIzol reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific,USA). The cDNA was synthesized with PrimeScript RT reagent kit (Takara, Otsu, Shiga, Japan) according to the manufacturer's protocol. PCR was performed on the LightCycler 96 Real-Time PCR System (Roche, Switzerland) using SYBR Green Master Mix kit (Roche, Switzerland). Primers specific for real-time quantitative PCR are listed in Table 1. For each reaction, 10 µl of SYBR Green Master Mix was used, 1.0 µl of each primer solution at 10 µM and 8 µl of diluted cDNA were added. PCR cycling protocol was as follows: initial 50 °C for 2 min, denaturation for 10 min at 95 °C, followed by 40 cycles at 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 1 min. The housekeeping gene Rps6 was used as an internal control and the data were analyzed with LightCycler 96 Software v1.1 (Roche, Switzerland). Quantitation of relative mRNA expression was calculated using 2−ΔΔCt method [34]. Each experiment was performed twice, shown here is a representative result.
